newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Ivorian premier urges EU to open its market.
newsitem.headline: Ivorian premier urges EU to open its market.

text.p: The European Union must open up its market to imports of industrial products from African countries, Ivory Coast Prime Minister Daniel Kablan Duncan said on Thursday.

"Trade barriers hinder a diversification of our exports, especially industrial products like textiles, and restrict us to shipping raw materials," Duncan told a conference organised by the Club de Bruxelles.

Duncan told the gathering on the promotion of West African economic and monetary union that if African countries were prepared to carry out painful economic restructuring programmes, industrial countries should do the same.
He called for the creation of a European export insurance scheme to provide financial support to help expand trade between Europe and Africa.
"The accent should be on trade not aid," Duncan told Reuters, noting that industrialised countries were finding it increasingly difficult to raise aid flows.

Duncan agreed with the European Commission's development aid commissioner Joao de Deus Pinheiro that greater effort should be made to encourage the private sector and make ACP countries more competitive in world markets.

On Wednesday, Deus Pinheiro presented a discussion paper on future relations between the EU and mainly African developing countries, stressing the need to use funds more efficiently and to make African countries more competitive.
The Commission is due next year to present proposals for a new Lome aid and trade pact, linking the 15-nation EU with 70 African, Caribbean and Pacific (ACP) developing countries,
Deus Pinheiro cited the Ivory Coast as one of Africa's successes, saying that economic growth was expected to reach 10 percent in 1998.
